**The Shy Robot Who Learned to Dance**

Once upon a time, in a shiny city full of whirring machines and blinking lights, lived a small robot named Rolly. Rolly had big, round eyes and a quiet heart. He loved to fix things and read stories, but when the music played, he’d hide behind a pile of old gears.

One day, the city announced a big dance party! Robots and robots-to-be would gather to show off their moves. Rolly’s friends all practiced every day, but Rolly didn’t know how to dance.

At first, Rolly just watched. He saw Twinkle the toaster spin in circles and Bumble the blender bounce up and down. But when it was his turn, Rolly stood still, too shy to move.

Feeling sad, Rolly asked his friend Pixel, a kind robot who loved dance, for help. Pixel smiled and said, “Dancing isn’t about being perfect. It’s about having fun and practicing.”

So every day after school, Rolly practiced. He wiggled his wheels, swayed his arms, and even bounced on his feet. He made silly mistakes, but he never gave up. He practiced with Pixel, then with Twinkle and Bumble, and soon, he was dancing all by himself!

On the big day, Rolly stepped onto the dance floor. He felt nervous, but then he remembered all his practice. He moved to the beat, and the crowd cheered!

Rolly had learned an important lesson: with practice, even the shyest robot can find their rhythm.

And from that day on, Rolly danced every night—because he knew the best way to be brave was to keep trying, just like he did with every step.

Urban beekeeping is the practice of raising honeybees in densely populated areas such as cities, towns, and suburbs. Tico had big, round eyes and a body made of soft silver metal, but he was too afraid to join the other robots when they danced in the moonlight. He watched them twirl and spin with joy, but Tico always stayed in the shadows, hiding behind a big pile of shiny parts.

One evening, as Tico peeked out from behind the pile, he saw a glowing butterfly land on his shoulder. It fluttered its wings and whispered, “Tico, you have a special kind of magic. You just need to find your rhythm.”
